items.reasoning: The literal N-1 bound for unconditional bounded-error classical randomized search is false, including for a label-symmetric/unbiased algorithm. Take n=2, N=4. Sample a uniform random permutation of the four inputs, query its first two distinct entries, and output the marked entry if either query hits. If both answers are0, choose uniformly from the remaining two inputs. For each fixed marked input, the hit probability is2/4; on the complementary event the final guess succeeds with probability1/2. Hence unconditional success is1/2+(1/2)(1/2)=3/4>1/2 using exactly2<N-1=3 queries in the worst case. The algorithm is equivariant under every permutation of input labels, with the same success for every mark, so it is not biased toward a particular candidate. I also executed a bounded exact enumeration: all24 permutations times the two final guess choices give36 successes out of48 for each of the four possible marks. Padding to a fixed distinct-query count is legitimate after caching/removing repeats, but does not fix the proof: after conditioning on a particular all-zero transcript, the remaining pair is indistinguishable and conditional success is at most1/2; hit transcripts have success1 and must be included in the unconditional probability. For randomized algorithms the pair of unqueried candidates also depends on the internal random choices, so choosing the adverse pair after fixing those choices swaps the standard worst-input/average-coins quantifiers. In general the same symmetric q-query construction succeeds with (q+1)/N, retaining the usual Omega(N) constant-success scale but not the stated exact N-1 threshold. N-1 is the exact-certainty/deterministic worst-case boundary, or a conditional-transcript statement under an expressly different success contract. The pinned Proposition11.1 and proof print this stronger erroneous claim; no definition of 'unbiased' there excludes the symmetric counterexample. Rubric3 and steps4–5 inherit the invalid inference. The separate observation that classical transcript indistinguishability alone supplies no quantum lower bound is correct, but cannot rescue the false classical theorem. No quantum lower-bound proof or production quantum execution is claimed.
